Build a Julia library from specific packages

Source: R/backend.R
build_library.Rd

Like install_backend(), but compiles only packages and writes the library to out, for package development. By default, it builds the package in the working directory into its .jlbind/ directory, which devtools::load_all() then uses instead of the library from install_backend(). To use a library written elsewhere, set JLBIND_LIBRARY to its path before loading the package.

Usage

build_library(
  packages = ".",
  out = NULL,
  julia = NULL,
  update = FALSE,
  develop = NULL
)

Arguments

packages

Names of installed packages, or paths to package sources or installed packages.

out

Directory to write the library to. Defaults to .jlbind/ in the sources of packages, which must then be a single source directory.

julia

Path to the julia executable. By default, the JULIA environment variable, or julia on the PATH.

update

If TRUE, use the newest dependency versions instead of those in the packages' Manifest.toml files.

develop

Paths to local Julia packages to use instead of their released versions.

Value

The path to the library, invisibly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In the sources of a package that uses jlbind
build_library()
devtools::load_all()

# Several packages, used through JLBIND_LIBRARY
lib <- build_library(c("pkg1", "pkg2"), "jlbind-lib")
Sys.setenv(JLBIND_LIBRARY = lib)
} # }
